- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.65) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.30), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 20–30 day horizon after recent spikes; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for lagged price recovery.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 5–7 days, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias in 30-day forecasts; if recent 10-day average is 1–2% below 30-day average, forecast should align with that average.
- Overshoots after spikes (e.g., +5%+ above peak) are common; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak unless sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral), model tends to be flat; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to avoid underperformance.
